summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, left flank pain radiating to the scrotum, and poor drainage from his left percutaneous nephrostomy (PCN) tube, three days after a minor assault. He had a history of neurogenic bladder with a left ureteral stricture managed by a PCN tube, and a recent admission for tube dislodgement. Initial evaluation revealed pyuria and bacteriuria, with urine cultures growing Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli, both sensitive to meropenem. Imaging showed the PCN tube was malpositioned, leading to inadequate drainage. The tube was successfully exchanged by interventional radiology, after which drainage improved and symptoms resolved. He was treated with intravenous meropenem, later transitioned to oral fosfomycin. Hypertension was managed with initiation of amlodipine. Lymphadenopathy in the left inguinal and cervical regions was noted but deemed non-concerning after normal LDH, uric acid, and imaging. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans and new prescriptions for amlodipine and naloxone due to chronic high-dose opioid use.
